What books do you reccomend for a personal library?

The thing about a personal library is that it is personal -- it reflects your personal reading interests. Every personal library will be different. However, there is a core of literature that everyone should be familiar with, and it should form a part of every well-rounded library. These are generally termed the "classics" because they are timeless. They are the books readers would not willingly let die. If you consult the "Harvard classics" list, sometimes called "Dr. Eliot's five-foot bookshelf," a collection originally put together to educate students of Harvard University when there were still intelligent minds at Harvard (alas, a thing of the past), you will find many of them.

Most of the great works are European because Europeans did the only writing that matters in past centuries. Other races scarcely rate a glance, although there are a handful of Chinese, Japanese and Indian works worth having. A library in the English language will naturally favor the history of English literature. You can't omit the ancient Greek dramatists, however, because so much of our civilization is based on Greek and Roman thought. After the Greeks, start with Chaucer, or Beowulf if you wish, and move on to Shakespeare and his fellow dramatists, Milton, Dr. Johnson's circle, the Romantics of the early 19th century, and the Victorian novelists and poets. You may, if you wish, continue beyond the Edwardian Period, but I wouldn't recommend it -- a dreadful lot, those later literary dim-bulbs.

In nonfiction you'll want to fill your shelves with the Greeks and Romans again, for their philosophy and history, and don't omit Gibbon's Decline and Fall or Burton's Anatomy of Melancholy, both essential works. As for the Americans ... well, enough said of the matter. If you must -- Melville, Poe, Hawthorne, Thoreau. Stay away from Longfellow, he'll give you indigestion every time. Dickenson is good in small doses.

So many shelves to fill, so little time. The world is your second-hand book store. Enjoy.
